newsitem.title: USA: Gold Banc likely to guide 1997 EPS view higher.
newsitem.headline: Gold Banc likely to guide 1997 EPS view higher.

text.p: Gold Banc Corp Chief Executive Michael Gullion on Monday said the bank holding company would likely guide analysts' estimates of its 1997 earnings higher than the current consensus of $0.65 a share.

"If we think we're going to significantly exceed market expectations then I think it's our duty and fudiciary responsibility to be updating the market place as a result," Gullion said in a telephone interview.
When asked if he expected the bank would be updating earnings guidance when second-quarter results are reviewed, he said, "more than likely, yes."
When asked if that meant he was likely to guide estimates higher, Gullion said, "Correct."
Gullion also said he expected to at least meet second-quarter estimates calling for Leawood, Kansas-based Gold Banc to have earnings of $0.15 a share before a one-time gain.
"We at least expect to do the estimates that are out there on the Street," Gullion said.

The full-year 1997 estimate compares with 1996 earnings of $0.71 a share, which was based on fewer shares because of the company's initial public offering in November. Second-quarter 1996 data is not comparable.
Gold Banc shares were unchanged at 13-7/8 Monday.
